parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish صایوان (sayvan, “awning, canopy, overhang”), from earlier سایبان (sayban), from Classical Persian سایبان (sâybân, sâyâbân, “parasol, umbrella; awning, overhang”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سفالت (sefâlet), from Classical Persian سَفَالَت (safālat), from Arabic سَفَالَة (safāla).

parole.significato: salamander, a long and slender amphibian of the order Caudata, superficially resembling a lizard
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سمندر (semender, “salamander”), from Classical Persian سَمَنْدَر (samandar, “salamander”), thought to be a compound of سام (sâm, “fire, flame”) + اندر (andar, “inside”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سر, from Classical Persian سر.

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سیر و سفر (seyr ü sefer), from Classical Persian سیر و سفر (sayr u safar, “travel”), from Arabic سَيْر (sayr, “movement, traffic”) and Arabic سَفَر (safar, “travel”). By surface analysis, seyir + ü + sefer.

parole.significato: smack, cuff, buffet, a slap delivered with the palm of the hand
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سله (sille), a vulgarized form of Classical Persian سیلی (sili, “slap on the face”).

parole.significato: craftsman who produces silver wires or threads
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سیمكش (simkeş), from Classical Persian سیمکش (sīm-kaš, “wire-drawer”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سپاهی, from Classical Persian سپاهی (sipāhī)

parole.significato: order (request for some product or service)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سپارش (sipariş), from Classical Persian سِپَارِش (sipāriš).
From Ottoman Turkish صوك بهار (son bahar), by surface analysis, son (“last”) + bahar (“spring”), from Classical Persian بهار (“spring”).

parole.significato: hyacinth, any bulbous flowering plant of the genus Hyacinthus
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish سنبل (sünbül), from Classical Persian سنبل (sunbul, “hyacinth”), ultimately from Arabic سُنْبُل (sunbul, “kind of aromatic plant”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish [script needed] (sünepe). Evliya Çelebi records this words from the dialect spoken by Corinthian Greeks. According to Ayverdi, from Classical Persian سُنْبَه (sunba).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ستون (sütun), from Classical Persian ستون (sutūn). Doublet of üstüvane.

parole.significato: scrofula, a form of tuberculosis tending to cause enlarged and degenerated lymph nodes
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish صراجه (sıraca, “scrofula”), itself from Classical Persian سِرَاجَه (sirāja, “kind of horse disease”).

parole.significato: Used with postpositions like dek, değin, kadar, beri etc. to emphasize the beginning or the end of a thing with regards…
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تا (tā), from Classical Persian تَا (tā, “up to, until”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تخت (taht), from Classical Persian تخت (taxt). See there for cognates.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تخته (tahta, “board, plank”), itself from Classical Persian تخته (taxta).

parole.significato: litter, any platform designed to carry a person or a load, like a sedan chair, hammock litter, etc.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تخت روان (taht-ı revân), from Classical Persian تَخْتِ رَوَان (taxt-i rawān). By surface analysis, taht (“throne”) + -i (ezafe suffix) + revan (“walking, going, itinerant”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish دارچین (tarçin, darçın), borrowed from Classical Persian دَارْچِین (dārčīn), from Old Persian 𐎭𐎠𐎽𐎢𐎺 (d-a-ru-u-v) or Sanskrit चीन (cīna).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تاسه, from Classical Persian تاسه.

parole.significato: tabar, a type of battle axe with a crescent-shaped blade, carried by some dervishes
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تبر (teber, “axe, hatchet; halberd”), from Classical Persian تبر (tabar, “axe, hatchet”).

parole.significato: chalk (used for drawing and for writing on a blackboard.)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish تباشیر (tebeşir), from Classical Persian تباشیر (tabāšīr, “chalk, clay, plaster; sugar from bamboo, tabasheer”) (perhaps borrowed from Hindi तबाशीर (tabāśīr, “tabasheer”)), ultimately from Sanskrit तवक्षीर (tavakṣīra, “white substance from bamboo, tabasheer”, literally “bark mil
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish دف (tef), from Classical Persian دف (daf), from Arabic دف (daff).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تكیه (tekye), from Classical Persian تَکْیَه (takya).

parole.significato: salaam, a low bow used as a ceremonial act of deference
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تمنا (temenna, “salaam”), from Classical Persian تمنا (tamannā, “wish, desire; entreaty, request”), from Arabic تَمَنَّى (tamannā, “to wish for, to desire”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تنقید (tenkid), from Classical Persian تَنْقِید (tanqīd), a pseudo-Arabism from the root ن ق د (n q d).

parole.significato: cress, garden cress, any fast-growing, edible herb of the species Lepidium sativum
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تره (tere, “cress”), from Classical Persian تره (tare, “garden herb; Iranian leek”).

parole.significato: handbarrow, a four-armed, wooden frame carried by two people, used for transporting materials in construction sites
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تسكره (teskere, “litter, stretcher, bier”), from earlier دسكره (deskere), from Classical Persian [Term?].
From Ottoman Turkish دستره (destere, testere), from Classical Persian دستره (dastara, “handsaw”), from دست (dast, “hand”) + اره (arra, “saw”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تستی (testi), variant of دستی (desti), from Classical Persian دستی (dasti).
From Ottoman Turkish تریاكی (tiryaki), from Classical Persian تِرْیَاک (tiryāk), from Ancient Greek θηριακή (thēriakḗ).

parole.significato: black francolin, any game bird of the species Francolinus francolinus, native to south and southwestern Asia
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish تراج (turac, “black francolin”), from Classical Persian تراج (torrâj), ultimately from Arabic دُرَّاج (durrāj, “francolin”).
From Ottoman Turkish ترنجی (türünci, turuncu), from Classical Persian ترنجی (turunji).

parole.significato: pickle, any vegetable preserved in vinegar and consumed as relish
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ترشی (turşı, turşu, “pickle”), from Classical Persian ترشی (turšī, “sourness; pickle”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish طرابزان (tarabizan), from Classical Persian داربزین (dārabzīn).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish استا (usta), derived from Classical Persian اوستا (ūstā).

parole.significato: An interjection expressing pity or upset.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish واه, Classical Persian وَاه (wāh).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish ویرانه (virane), from Classical Persian وَیرَانَه (wayrāna).

parole.significato: yakhni, any of various stocks, broths and stews made with meat and cooked with onions
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish یخنی (yahni, “stew of meat or fish”), from Classical Persian یَخْنِی (yaxnī), possibly from Sogdian yxnyy (yaxnī).

From earlier hemyan kesici, likely through folk-etymological reanalysis of the first component as yan (“side”), itself from Classical Persian همیان (hamyān, “money belt”), from میان (miyān, “waist”); the second component from kes- (“to cut”) + -ci (occupation suffix). Partial doublet of meydan, meya

parole.significato: jasmine, any of several flowering plants of the genus Jasminum, mostly native to Asia
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish یاسمین (yasemin), from Classical Persian یَاسَمِین (yāsamīn), a variant of یاسمن (yâsaman, “jasmine”), ultimately from Middle Persian 𐭩𐭠𐭮𐭬𐭭𐭠 (yʾsmn' /⁠yāsaman⁠/, “jasmine”).
From Ottoman Turkish یَگانه (“just, only”), from Classical Persian یَگَانَه (yagāna, “unique”).

parole.significato: jade, jadestone, a semi-precious stone generally green or white in color
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish یشم (yeşm, yeşem, “jasper; jade”), from Classical Persian یشم (yašm, “jasper”). Perhaps underwent a merger with yeşil (“green”), alluding to the color of the gem.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish یاران (yâran), from Classical Persian یاران (yārān). Doublet of yâren.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish یاران (yâran), from Classical Persian یاران (yārān). Doublet of yâran.

Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish ظَالِم (zalım), from Classical Persian ظَالِم (zālim), from Arabic ظَالِم (ẓālim). Cognate with Gagauz zulum, Azerbaijani zalım and zalim. Used in Turkish since the 14th century.

parole.significato: time (progression into the future with the passing of present and past events)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish زمان (zamân), from Old Anatolian Turkish زمان (zamân), from Classical Persian زَمَان (zamān)

parole.significato: lily, any of several flowering plants in the genus Lilium
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زنبق (zambak), from Classical Persian زنبق (zanbaq), from Arabic زَنْبَق (zanbaq), from Middle Persian [script needed] (cmbk' /⁠čambak⁠/), from Sanskrit चम्पक (campaka).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زبان (zeban), from Classical Persian زَبَان (zabān).
From Ottoman Turkish زمین (zamin), from Classical Persian زمین (zamīn, “earth, Earth”), cognate with Latin humus, Ancient Greek χθών (khthṓn)).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زنگین (zengin), from Classical Persian سَنْگِین (sangīn). Largely replaced native bay, now limited to dialectal use.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زردهچال, from earlier زرده چاو, ultimately from Classical Persian [Term?]. Compare Persian زردچوبه.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زرین (zerrin, “golden”), from Classical Persian زَرِّین (zarrīn, “golden”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زرزوات (zarzavat, zerzevat), from earlier سبزوات (sebzevât), from Classical Persian سَبْزَوَاتْ (sabzawāt, “vegetables”), whence also Tajik сабзавот (sabzavot). Compare Uzbek sabzavot (“vegetable”).

parole.significato: thumb ring, a special ring worn on the interphalangeal crease of the thumb to protect it while drawing the string of a…
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زهكیر (zihgir, zehgir, “an archer's thumb stall”), from Classical Persian زهگیر (zihgir), from زه (zih, “bowstring”) + گیر (gir, “that which holds; block, obstacle”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زنجیر (zincir), from Classical Persian زَنْجِیر (zanjīr).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زندان (zindân), borrowed from Classical Persian زندان (zindān), from Middle Persian [script needed] (zyndʾn').
From Ottoman Turkish زنهار (zinhar), from Classical Persian زِنْهَار (zinhār).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زیرا (zira, “because”), from Classical Persian زیرا (zīrā).

parole.significato: lovelock, a long lock of hair, often plaited, worn apart from the hair that remains
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زلف (zülf, zülüf), from Classical Persian زلف (zulf, “curl, tress”).

parole.significato: punch, puncheon, a device used for creating holes in thin material, or to stamp or emboss a mark or design on a surface
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish زنبه (zınba, zımba, “punch, stapler”), from Classical Persian سنبه (sunba, “punch, wimble”).

parole.significato: jackal, any of certain wild canids of the genera Lupulella and Canis, specifically Canis aureus
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چقال (çakal), from Classical Persian شغال (šaġâl), from Sanskrit सृगाल (sṛgāla, “jackal”), from Proto-Indo-Aryan *śr̥gālás, a suffixed derivative of Proto-Indo-Iranian *ćárguš (“predatory animal”).

parole.significato: castanet, a percussion instrument consisting of a pair of concave shell-shaped parts joined on one edge
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چالپاره (çalpara), from Classical Persian چَار (čār, “four”, colloquial form of چَهَار (čahār)) + پَارَه (pāra, “part”).

parole.significato: pergola, arbor, a framework used to support and train climbing plants
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چارطاق (çardak), from Classical Persian چَارْطَاق (čārtāq, “vault”), a compound of چار (čâr, “four”) + طاق (tâq, “arch”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چاره (çare, “remedy”), from Old Anatolian Turkish چاره (çāre), from Classical Persian چَارَه (čāra).

parole.significato: rye, any grass of the species Secale cereale or its grain
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چاودار (çavdar, “rye”), from Classical Persian جَوْدَرْ (jawdar, “rye”).

parole.significato: paddy, rough or unhusked rice, either before it is milled or as a crop to be harvested
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چلتیك (çeltik), from Classical Persian شلتوک (šaltôk, “rice still in the husk; rice-hull”), a compound of شالی (šâli, “rice hull”) + توک (tôk, “bundle, fagot; handle, grip”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چنبر (çenber), itself from Classical Persian چَنْبَر (čanbar, “circle, hoop”)

parole.significato: the inner surface or partition of a wall, trench, etc.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چپر (çeper, “fence”), from Classical Persian چپر (čapar, “circle, ring; palisade”).

parole.significato: frame, mount, any rigid, rectangular mounting for paintings, mirrors, slate, etc.
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چرچوه (çerçeve, “frame”), from Classical Persian چهار (“four”) + چوب (čôb, “stick”). Compare Northern Kurdish çarçove (“frame”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چیرك (çeyrek), from Classical Persian چاریک (čāryak, “one of four; a fourth”). Cognate with Kazakh ширек (šıyrek, “quarter”), Bashkir сирек (sirek, “quarter”), Uzbek chorak (“quarter”), etc.
From Classical Persian چَشِیدَن (čašīdan) or its stem چش (čaš). Compare Azerbaijani çeşid.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چشنی, from Classical Persian چَاشْنِی (čāšnī).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چركین (çirkin), from Classical Persian چِرْکِین (čirkīn), from چِرْک (čirk), itself a Turkic borrowing from Proto-Common Turkic *čirik (whence çürük), ultimately from Proto-Turkic *čiri-, whence çürü-. Doublet of çürük
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چوبان (çoban), from Classical Persian چوپَان (čōpān), from Middle Persian 𐫢𐫇𐫁𐫀𐫗 (šwbʾn /⁠šubān⁠/), ultimately from Old Persian *fšupāna.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چوربا (çorba), from Classical Persian شورْبَا (šōrbā). Cognate with Azerbaijani şorba, Kazakh сорпа (sorpa), Kyrgyz шорпо (şorpo), Romanian ciorbă.

parole.significato: packing needle, a large needle used in sewing up canvas packages or sacks
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چوالدوز (çuvalduz, çuvaldız), itself from Classical Persian جُوَال دُوز (juwāl dūz, “packing needle”).

parole.significato: beet, a cultivated, flowering plant of the species Beta vulgaris
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چوكندر (çükündür), from Classical Persian چغندر (čuġundur, “beet”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چفوت (çıfut), from Classical Persian جهود (jahūd, juhūd, “Jew”).

parole.significato: planetree, especially the oriental plane (Platanus orientalis)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چِنَار (çınâr), borrowed from Classical Persian چِنَار (činār), from Middle Persian cynʾl (/⁠činār⁠/).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چراقمان (çırakman), from older Ottoman Turkish چراقمه (çırakma). From Classical Persian چراغپا.
From Ottoman Turkish امید (ümîd), from Classical Persian امید (umīḏ).

parole.significato: expert (person with extensive knowledge or ability)
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish استاد, borrowed from Classical Persian اُسْتَاد (ustād), from earlier اُوسْتَاد (ūstād).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اصمارلامق, from Classical Persian سِپُرْدَن (sipurdan). By surface analysis, ısmar + -la.

parole.significato: spinach, any flowering plant of the species Spinacia oleracea and its edible leaves
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اسپناق (ıspanak), from Classical Persian اسپناخ (ispanāx). For the phonetic change, compare Turkmen ysmanak.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اِضْطِرَاب (ıztırâb), from Classical Persian اِضْطِرَاب (iztirāb), from Arabic اِضْطِرَاب (iḍṭirāb, “disturbance; disorder”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شادان (şadan), from Classical Persian شادان (šâdân), from Classical Persian شاد (šâd).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شاه (şah), from Classical Persian شاه (šāh, “king”).

parole.significato: royal, regal, kingly, befitting of a monarch
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شاهانه (şahane), from Classical Persian شاهانه (šāhāna). By surface analysis, şah (“king, shah”) + -ane (adjective-forming suffix).

parole.significato: buzzard, buteo, any of several birds of prey in the genus Buteo
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شاهین (şahin, “peregrine falcon”), from Classical Persian شاهین (šāhīn, “falcon”), ultimately from Middle Persian [script needed] (*šāhēn, literally “majestic, kingly”).

parole.significato: fumitory, any herbaceous flowering plant of the genus Fumaria, specifically Fumaria officinalis
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شاهتره (şahtere), from Classical Persian شاهتره (šâhtare). By surface analysis, şah (“shah”) + tere (“garden cress”).

parole.significato: wallflower, any of several herbs and flowers in the genus Erysimum, especially Erysimum cheiri
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شببوی (şebboy, “wallflower; stock”), from Classical Persian شببوی (šab-bôy, “wallflower; stock”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شبنم, from Classical Persian شَبْنَم (šabnam).
From Ottoman Turkish شفتالو (şeftalı, şeftali), from Old Anatolian Turkish شفتالو (şeftalü, şeftali), from Classical Persian شفتالو (šaftālū).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شهر (şehir), from Classical Persian شَهْر (šahr).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شربت (şerbet), borrowed from Classical Persian شَرْبَت (šarbat), borrowed from Arabic شَرْبَة (šarba), from شَرِبَ (šariba).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شلته, borrowed from Classical Persian چِلْتَه (čilta).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شیرین, from Classical Persian شیرین (šērēn).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شیشه (şişe), from Old Anatolian Turkish شیشه (şīşä), borrowed from Classical Persian شِیشَه (šīša), from Middle Persian [script needed] (šyšk' /⁠šīšag⁠/, “bottle, flask”).
From Ottoman Turkish شناو, from Classical Persian شِنَاو (šināw). Compare Iranian Persian شِنا (šenâ) with the same meaning.
From Ottoman Turkish شیره (şıre, şıra), from Classical Persian شِیرَه (šīra).
